title: Naturality of the tensor ideal-power quotient equivalence
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, n a natural number, and f:M to N an A-linear map. The ordinary equivalences (A/I^n) tensor_A M = M/I^nM and (A/I^n) tensor_A N = N/I^nN commute with extension of scalars of f and the quotient map Q_n(f) from [def-sf-adic-module-quotient-data]. Thus for every tensor x, e_N((1 tensor f)(x)) = Q_n(f)(e_M(x)). No positivity, finiteness, or nontriviality assumption is needed.

source.place: section-tensor-product, Tag 03EK, ordinary tensor functoriality used in the constant quotient comparison. The algebraic equivalence and generator formula are Mathlib LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Quotient.lean, quotTensorEquivQuotSMul and quotTensorEquivQuotSMul_mk_tmul.

proof.text: Apply tensor induction. At zero and at sums, both sides agree by linearity. For a pure tensor, lift its quotient-ring scalar along A to A/I^n. The generator formula for quotTensorEquivQuotSMul gives the quotient classes of a times f(x) and f(a times x); these coincide by A-linearity of f. This includes n=0 and degenerate rings, ideals, and modules.

lean.statement:
theorem adicPerfectTensorQuotient_naturality
    {A : Type w} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (n : ℕ)
    {M N : ModuleCat.{w} A} (f : M ⟶ N)
    (x : (ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n))).obj M) :
    TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul N (I ^ n)
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n))).map f).hom x) =
      ((AdicCohomology.quotient I n).map f)
        (TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M (I ^ n) x)
